title: a tag search starting at the opening tag let the hashed length underflow to SIZE_MAX
object: the key buffer the filter is handed, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a length computed as a pointer difference that underflows when the two pointers coincide
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/realloc, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: 1.6.45:proxy_lua.c carries `memchr(t1+1, conf[1], remain-1)` (`grep -c` = 1). The pre-fix form, searching from `t1` with the full `remain`, is at 212c3820c7bb^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x1025ac, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x102578` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- this is not a slab chunk and not a cache.c object -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the crossing is not bounded at all: the length handed to the hasher is (size_t)-1 rather than a few bytes too many, so this row's magnitude is the whole address space. It is also the only row here whose trigger is a CONFIGURATION -- a two-character tag whose characters are equal.
